recipes.name: Jerre's Black Bean and Pork Tenderloin Slow Cooker Chili
ingredients_raw: 1.5 pounds pork tenderloin, cut into 2 inch strips
1 small red bell pepper, coarsely chopped

steps.text: Combine pork tenderloin, onion, red pepper, black beans, salsa, chicken broth, oregano, cumin, and chili powder in a slow cooker. Set to Low and cook for 8 to 10 hours.
Break up pieces of cooked pork to thicken the chili before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Jerre's Black Bean and Pork Tenderloin Slow Cooker Chili
raw_recipe.description: Tender pork and black beans stew all day in your slow cooker. Just combine the ingredients, set the cooker to low, and 8 to 10 hours later enjoy a rich and delicious chili.

review.reviewBody: This was very good. I did make a few changes. My husband, a Chef, said you should use loin and not tenderloin. I used a loin roast and was perfect. I added cumin, coriander, a dark beer (fat tire, my favorite), and a spoon full of peanut butter. Sounds strange, but you only want enough fot the nutty flavor, helps bring out the flavors of the beans. Added hot sauce too. Severed over lime flavor chips, toped with black sour cream, cheese and black olives. To me, it was almost a gormet natchos not a chili, but the word chili is different in every place. I think I would take the lid off for an hour, to much liquid or add a little less broth, or even less beer, can always drink what you don't use, right.

Jerre’s recipe is a great idea and a good basis for making it your own. As is, I think it would be too bland. I gathered suggestions from other reviewers and it was a huge 5 star success. Hot enough to make my husband’s nose run, but not too hot for me with added cheese and sour cream. 

I served it over brown rice in a bowl lined around the edges with Lime Tortilla chips. Next time I’d just use regular tortilla chips for scooping. We squeezed a little lime over the chili and that was enough. It was a little soupy, but fine over rice and I think it will thicken up. If not, it’s still good.

I started the crockpot on low at 8:45 a.m for about an hour, upped it to high for about 3 hours and back to low until we ate around 6:00 p.m.

I used a 1.6 lb package of thick boneless pork chops and increased the seasonings a little to account for that. I cut them in large cubes which were hard to shred, but I liked the chunks of meat too.

I substituted one can of corn for a can of beans (all drained). 
I kept the onion and the red pepper the same and used medium salsa. 
My additions: 4 oz can of mild green chopped chiles, 14.5 oz can of fire roasted diced tomatoes with Adobo seasoning, 3 Tbs minced garlic from a jar (equivalent to 3 cloves). 
I used 2 chicken bouillon cubes and 1/2 c of ale instead of chicken broth (we drank the remainder of the ale with the chili). Yum!

It’s a keeper.

Thank you so much for this recipe! It is so good! Only changes I made were a three bean mix of pinto beans, dark red kidney beans and black beans. And I added some chopped jalapeno. The pork tenderloin I used was 2.3 pounds. So a meatier chili. And I left it whole in the Crock-Pot til it was time to serve then I shredded it. I have a newer fast cooking crock pot like so many others of us do but since my pork tenderloin was still a little bit Frozen I definitely cooked it 10 hours on low. Served with a little sour cream some cheddar cheese and corn tortilla chips. Loved it and can't wait to use the leftovers for quesadillas or tacos and freeze the rest! Thanks Jerre!
This is a good tasting chili! I made it according to the instructions. I also added a teaspoon of chopped garlic and a half teaspoon of cayenne pepper.

Delicious! As others suggested, I used a pork roast rather than tenderloin, and that worked great. Cooked on low for 9 hours, it just fell apart. I also added a can of diced tomatoes and a can of diced green chilis. It got rave reviews at my office crockpot potluck. Thanks so much for sharing your recipe!

This is an absolutely fabulous dish! I added two types of mild peppers plus fresh garlic, cilantro and parsley and slow cooked it for only 3.5 hours to achieve a thickness proper for serving over rice. This is the type of recipe that opens up to many individual flavors and seasonings. I look forward to experimenting in the future!

Loved this chili! Used 4 pork loins which I forgot to chop up but no need as they literally fell apart when finished cooking. Upped spices as suggested (2 tsp cumin, 1/2 cup fresh cilantro near end of cooking time). I didn't have an onion so left that out and added 2 cloves garlic. Also subbed 1 cup dried black turtle beans for the canned and added 1 can kidney beans and chopped tomatoes instead of the salsa. The flavor was great and oregano worked surprisingly well! Next time may add some corn.

First time using pork loin for such a recipe and it was tasty and good! Only used one drained three-bean can instead of three cans of beans; personally, that would have been too much. Also added a small can of corn, drained. I think if I used a whole loin instead of cutting it into pieces first, it would have cooked up just as good and shredded well too. It came out like a stew, but by the next day wasn’t as liquidy. Hubby liked it, as did I, so will make it again!

My family enjoyed this recipe. I did use 3/4 cup of chicken broth and this didn't seem to cause any issues - there was lots of liquid. I also put in 2 onions as it is quite a large recipe for only a small onion. I felt it was lacking salt, despite the chicken broth. The recipe doesn't call for it. It was a little bland without it. I would add 1 tsp for starters next time.

We loved this chili. I wanted to have everything ready to put into slow cooker very early in the AM before work so I cut meat up the night before and mixed in with salsa, onion and peppers, and spices, and placed in refrigerator.. In the morning I put everything in cooker with 2 cans of black beans. I was concerned because of some comments about to many beans. When I came home from work, I added another can of beans and some jalapeños and cooked for a couple more hours.Meat shredded beautifully. So easy. I willl definitely make again. Total cook time was about 8 hrs.
This is a great recipe and everyone loved it. I added two stalks of celery and a can of medium diced chilis. I only had a small tenderloin so I added sliced smoke sausage.
Was delicious! I made no changes to the recipes.

This was a great base recipe. I used leftover roasted pork loin with sautéed Anaheim peppers and yellow onion. I had no clack beans so I used 2 15 oz cans of chili beans and added a dash of cayenne for heat.
Added sweet potato and fresh corn kernels. Delicious
I added roasted sweet potatoes. Great addition with this flavor combination.
Was very easy to prepare...the only thing I would do differently is to use "Hot" Salsa...so it is hotter.

I had no pork tenderloin but I did have one of those big 24 oz. cans of USDA pork w/its juices, so I dumped in the whole can, juices & all, because I knew I'd be draining & rinsing the black beans (the liquid in canned beans grosses me out), so I knew I'd need to replace some of that liquid and the pork juices would also add great flavor). It was good but like many ppl said, more of a soup & a bit bland, so after reading the comments about the ingredients some ppl added, I added a small can of tomato paste w/water, and then dumped in a bunch of tomato juice, a BUNCH of extra chili powder and lots of extra cumin, then seasoned it all w/Kosher salt. I will certainly make it again but with my own additions.
My husband loved this and he's extremely picky!
